name: Cheesy salmon & broccoli egg bake — optimized

source.author: Optimized version of cheesy_salmon_broccoli_bake
source.notes: Optimized version of cheesy_salmon_broccoli_bake, adopted per user request. Changes: light mozzarella instead of full-fat, heavy cream dropped (eggs set fine without it), broccoli doubled to 400 g. Same salmon (250 g), eggs (5–6), cherry tomatoes, seasoning and bake. 4 servings. Estimate.

ingredients.note: doubled — more fibre, folate and volume

steps: Preheat to 190 °C and line a baking dish.
Boil the broccoli 3–4 min in salted water; drain well.
Spread broccoli and salmon cubes in the dish.
Whisk eggs, salt, pepper and oregano; pour over.
Top with halved cherry tomatoes and the mozzarella.
Bake 25–30 min until set, salmon cooked through and the top golden. Cool slightly before slicing.

batch_totals.note: Whole bake (4 servings), optimized. Vs the original: ~46 kcal and ~6.6 g fat less per serving, a little more protein, nearly double the fibre, more folate and vitamin C — with the salmon's omega-3 and vitamin D untouched.

him.verdict: Keeps every strength of the original — ~33 g protein, ~1.1 g omega-3 and ~300 IU vitamin D per serving (sperm-priority micros), selenium and choline from eggs — while cutting the 'empty' fat (light mozzarella, no cream) and doubling the broccoli for fibre and vitamin C. ~9.5 g protein per 100 kcal.
flags: ~32 g protein, very low carb (~6 g)
~1.1 g omega-3 + ~300 IU vitamin D per serving (sperm micros)
high fat (~27 g) — salmon (good) + full-fat mozzarella (lever)

her_preconception.verdict: Even better for her than the original: same low-mercury DHA + vitamin D from salmon and choline from eggs, now with more folate and vitamin C from the doubled broccoli. Bake until the custard is fully set and the salmon opaque.
prenatal_highlights: DHA + vitamin D (salmon) — fetal brain development

safety_advisories.note: Bake until the custard is fully set and the salmon is opaque throughout — no runny egg or undercooked fish in pregnancy.
safety_advisories.swap: add a few minutes if the centre is soft

suggested_mods: No changes needed — a strong prenatal dish

cooking_guide: Drain the blanched broccoli very well (even pat it dry) — wet broccoli makes the custard watery.
Cut the salmon into even ~2–3 cm cubes so it cooks at the same rate as the custard sets.
Season the egg mix properly — eggs need salt to taste of anything — but go lighter if using salty cheese.
Spread everything in a single even layer so the custard surrounds it rather than pooling.
Bake until the centre is set (no wobble) and a knife comes out clean; check at 25 min.
Rest 5 min before slicing so it holds together.
adopted_note: Adopted 2026-11-07 (optimized). Per serving (of 4, ~290 g): ~351 kcal, 33.2 g protein, 20.2 g fat, 2.9 g fibre, ~1.1 g omega-3, ~504 mg sodium. him 9 / her 9. Standing spec: light mozzarella, no cream, 400 g broccoli. Bake until fully set.
